# 23. Finger-pad friction during viscous liquid spreading

tribology and biomechanics.

The practical question is friction dependence on viscosity, speed, load, and hydration.

`raw/` contains unchanged source downloads. `context/` contains source documentation, metadata snapshots and clearly labeled acquisition notes. Original archives are retained; temporary read-only inspection did not leave an extracted duplicate.

Ten source files combine raw finger position/force trials, friction summaries, viscosity versus shear rate, film-height records, hydration and finger-pad area. DAT tables have three header rows: variable, unit, comment.

Selection: Complete source record unless otherwise specified.

Measurements: Acquisition dates not established from the public record; publication field 2025-05-08, deposit creation 2025-05-21.

Release/version: 15365365; source publication field 2025-05-08.

Processing level: Force/position exports coexist with computed friction and supplied power-law fit parameters. Area was measured from calibrated photographs in ImageJ; hydration is a corneometer instrument scale (0–120), not percent water.

Source: [Finger-pad friction during viscous liquid spreading](https://zenodo.org/records/15365365). Reuse: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Source limitations and citation details are in `context/SOURCE_NOTES.md` and `PROVENANCE.json`.

The source files retain their original missing codes, calibration information, quality flags, labels and directory structure. No normalization, imputation, denoising, resampling or scientific format conversion has been performed. This folder is a research input, not evidence of a newly discovered principle.
note: Native source hashes, not a copy of upstream files. Prepared derivatives retain source terms; all publication/industrial-use decisions require those terms.
